entries.reason: Plan catalog data table (36 families / 239 ops) is pure data, not logic: it keeps the when/not/sk metadata and op lists human-readable in one file, so it carries the documented 600-line budget exemption. This replaces the removed runtime/catalog.ts ghost entry; the budget gate reads this registry instead of an inline allowlist.

Aggregation barrel for the catalog domain (data / tools / commands / logic). runtime/engine.ts and runtime/ internal callers need one stable import path per domain; the barrel holds no logic of its own, and the public facade registry (config/facades.json) records the four exports actually consumed through it.

The single documented src/ -> lib/runtime boundary: host-side code imports the built runtime entry points through this one file instead of scattering lib/ paths. Keeping the bridge as one re-export file is the boundary convention recorded in docs/architecture.md.

Split barrel for the headless receipt helpers (split / normalize / format). Callers and tests import the receipt surface from this single path; the module files keep the implementation and unit tests target them directly.

Cross-package reuse of private helpers from integrations/*_client.py predates the addon package split. The names stay private until those modules are next touched; the pytest private-import contract ties this registry entry to the real import graph so the entry cannot go stale.

Layered configuration (built-in default -> package -> home -> DSH_BLENDER_CONFIG -> DSH_BLENDER_PLUGIN_CONFIG -> per-item env -> auto-detection) keeps every layer, source label, warning and derived CFG field in one module so the resolution order is auditable in a single place. Splitting would scatter the precedence chain that doctor and tests assert on.

The queue manager owns submission, lease/slot accounting, cache hit handling, staging promotion and job lifecycle in one state machine; the render-pass cache additions need the same state transitions, and a split would duplicate that transaction boundary.
Host-local vision dispatch keeps the eight op validators, the DNN gate order, model checks and structured error mapping together so the error precedence is readable and testable as one table.

The managed Python/OpenCV installer is one state machine (discover -> create venv -> lock -> pip -> verify -> state.json) and a split would spread the lock/retry/atomic-rename invariants across files.

The vision worker manager keeps protocol framing, idle reaping, crash restart and the two-phase DNN hot-apply switch in one owner; the in-flight/pending revision bookkeeping must stay atomic in one module.

vision_pass is a self-contained manifest reader/decoder (depth/normal/object_index/alpha, per-frame and aggregate metrics, bounded outputs); keeping the decode and aggregation rules together keeps the units and formulas reviewable against render-pass-script.ts.

The runtime.json snapshot schema, revision monotonicity, env lock and runtime-state.json transition writer form one config state machine consumed by both the host RPC and the Gateway reconciler; splitting would separate the schema from the atomic write.

The owner-only /dsh-blender dnn RPC keeps apply/status/cancel-pending/rollback/download/probe in one handler so the runtime.json write, monotonic revision, forced reconcile and gateway_unreachable fallback share one transaction boundary; splitting would duplicate the write ordering the integration tests assert on.

DNN probe is a one-shot availability probe whose lifecycle (candidate normalization, interpreter resolution, spawn/timer/stdio/close handling, result assembly) stays in one module so the 10 s timeout, 1 MiB stdout cap, exit-code handling and check merging share one transaction boundary; splitting the probe process state machine from candidate/interpreter resolution would duplicate the invariants the probe tests assert on.
